article_notes: 330 working dogs from organised kennels across India suspected of babesiosis; 51 nested-PCR positive (47 B. gibsoni, 4 B. vogeli by sequencing). The authors split the 51 into three groups of 17 by clinical severity: group-1 apparently healthy (subclinical carriers), group-2 uncomplicated, group-3 complicated (cerebral/epilepsy, jaundice, renal failure, septic shock/DIC with death, MODS with death). Tables 3 and 4 give only the number of dogs per group with values above, below or within the reference range; no statistical tests and no means. All rows are descriptive_only. Table 3 platelet row is internally inconsistent (increased 2+1+0 but total 5). Group membership partly reflects the markers themselves (anaemia, jaundice, renal failure). No healthy-control comparisons. Samples were collected at kennels and sent to CMVL Meerut; timing relative to treatment not stated.

severity_definitions.definition: Three groups of 17 nested-PCR-positive dogs classified by clinical severity: subclinical carriers, mild uncomplicated babesiosis, complicated babesiosis (epilepsy/cerebral, jaundice, renal failure, septic shock with DIC and death, MODS and death). 5 of the 17 complicated dogs died.
severity_definitions.quote: dogs manifesting mild symptoms of simple or uncomplicated babesiosis (group-2) and lastly, dogs manifesting symptoms of complicated babesiosis (group-3)
